source_text: God cwæð ðā sōðlice, “Bēon nū lēoht on ðǣre heofonan fæstnesse, and tōdǣlen dæg and niht, and bēon tō tācnum, and tō tīdum, and tō dagum, and tō gēarum. And hīe scīnen on ðǣre heofonan fæstnesse, and ālīehten ðā eorðan”; hit wæs ðā swā geworden. And God geworhte twā miclu lēoht: ðæt māre lēoht tō ðæs dæges līehtinge, and ðæt lǣsse lēoht tō ðǣre niht līehtinge; and steorran hē geworhte. And gesętte hīe on ðǣre heofonan, ðæt hīe scinen ofer eorðan, and gīemden ðæs dæges and ðǣre niht, and tōdǣlden lēoht and ðīestru; God geseah ðā ðæt hit gōd wæs. And wæs geworden ǣfen and męrgen se fēorða dæg.

independent_source_translation.origin: New editorial source-audit translation made from the actual Old English; not learner prose or a task key.
independent_source_translation.text: God then said, “Let there now be lights in the firmament of heaven, and let them separate day and night, and let them be for signs, for seasons, for days, and for years. And let them shine in the firmament of heaven and illuminate the earth”; it then came to pass thus. And God made two great lights: the greater light for the illumination of the day, and the lesser light for the illumination of the night; and he made stars. And he set them in heaven, so that they might shine over the earth, rule over the day and the night, and separate light and darkness; God then saw that it was good. And evening and morning came to pass, the fourth day.
notes: sōðlice is a narrative connective here (source note15: Latin autem), not a compulsory emphatic claim “truly”. The English opening absorbs this connective.
“Let there be” renders a finite plural wish, not an infinitive. Each coordinated optative belongs to the wish or later purpose construction.
“Be for signs/seasons...” can idiomatically become “serve as signs...” but that is an English paraphrase, not an extra Old English verb.
The paired greater and lesser lights are unnamed in this source span. Do not replace them in the transcript or translation with sun and moon.
The closing source order and resultative formula are kept distinct from the simpler independent copula system. An idiomatic “there came evening and morning, the fourth day” preserves the sequence.
The final clauses say that the lights rule over day/night and divide light/darkness. They do not merely restate illumination.

construction_dependencies.analysis_and_limit: Direct speech introduced by supplied cwæð, with then and connective sōðlice. Unit2 productive quotation was specifically with sęcgan.
construction_dependencies.required_local_support: God cwæð ðā sōðlice = God then said; sōðlice is connective here (Latin autem).

construction_dependencies.analysis_and_limit: Plural finite optatives express a wish/command. Bēon is not an infinitive; all coordinated verbs share the lights as subject.
construction_dependencies.required_local_support: Bēon/bēon = let there be/let them be; tōdǣlen = let them separate; scīnen = let them shine; ālīehten = let them illuminate. These are actual supplied forms, with the complete wish explained.

construction_dependencies.analysis_and_limit: on governs dative fæstnesse; ðǣre heofonan is embedded genitive feminine singular, from weak heofone.
construction_dependencies.required_local_support: on ðǣre heofonan fæstnesse = in the firmament of heaven. Mark heofonan genitive and fæstnesse dative explicitly; ðǣre agrees with heofonan.

construction_dependencies.analysis_and_limit: tō + dative expresses assigned function/purpose. Noun cells are prior; this prepositional use is not taught by Unit2 tō wyrceanne.
construction_dependencies.required_local_support: tō tācnum/tīdum/dagum/gēarum = for signs/seasons/days/years; tō ... līehtinge = for the illumination of ...; genitive day/night is nested inside the dative phrase.

construction_dependencies.analysis_and_limit: Resultative fulfillment formula; prior wæs form does not establish independent perfect/resultative syntax.
construction_dependencies.required_local_support: hit wæs ðā swā geworden = it then came to pass thus / it was then so; geworden is supplied.

construction_dependencies.analysis_and_limit: Count-luminary lēoht at7/51/54/62 is a new sense; plural cells move from recognition to production. Token91 is prior mass light. New strong adjective, comparative, and numeral agreement under Unit3 grammar audit.
gesętte has omitted God/he subject; hīe is accusative plural object. on ðǣre heofonan has dative feminine singular heofonan, not genitive.

construction_dependencies.analysis_and_limit: ðæt introduces purpose; scinen, gīemden, tōdǣlden are past optatives. This is not the content-that sense.

construction_dependencies.analysis_and_limit: ofer eorðan means over the earth. Source spelling eorðan is compatible with accusative or dative singular; do not require one uniquely.

construction_dependencies.analysis_and_limit: gīeman governs genitive in this exact construction, explicitly documented by §156f. Genitive forms themselves are prior.
construction_dependencies.required_local_support: gīemden ðæs dæges and ðǣre niht = might rule over the day and the night. Here the verb governs the two genitives; this is not an of-relationship between nouns.

construction_dependencies.analysis_and_limit: Supplied strong geseah plus content clause ðæt hit gōd wæs. New predicate-adjective morphology can be observed within supplied content-clause syntax.
construction_dependencies.required_local_support: God geseah ðā ðæt hit gōd wæs = God then saw that it was good. ðæt is a conjunction, not the article; do not require independent subordinate-clause production.

construction_dependencies.analysis_and_limit: Closing resultative formula and source word order supplied. The new ordinal fēorða agrees with dæg; męrgen is a source vowel variant of selected morgen.
construction_dependencies.required_local_support: And wæs geworden ǣfen and męrgen se fēorða dæg = and evening and morning came to pass, the fourth day. Explain the complete formula without grading an invented unique compound-subject agreement rule.
